title: 2 Queens Lose??: A Rook and Pawn King Hunt
summary: Play the Black side: use a rook check to drive the king into two pawn checks before the extra queens can help.

nodes.question: How can Black keep checking despite White’s two queens?
nodes.explanation: Rh1+ forces Kg4. Then f5+ forces Kh5, where g6 delivers mate. White’s queens on b8 and d8 cannot answer these adjacent rook and pawn checks.

branches.title: Source finish: rook check, then two pawn checks
commentary: Black moves after Kxh3. White has two queens, but the exposed king must answer the immediate checks before using them.
Rh1+ brings the rook from e1 onto the king’s h-file. Rf2 controls g2/h2 and the second rank, while White’s own rook occupies h4.
Kg4 is White’s sole legal reply. The king steps off the h-file but enters a square attacked by an advancing f-pawn.
f5+ checks with the pawn from f6. Rf2 supports the pawn up the f-file, so the king cannot capture it.
Kh5 is White’s sole legal reply. The h6 pawn controls g5; Rf2 controls the f-file; Rh1 controls h3; and the white rook occupies h4.
g6# checks Kh5 with the pawn. Kh7 protects both g6 and h6, f5 controls g4, h6 controls g5, and White’s own rook blocks h4. The extra queens cannot interpose against a pawn’s adjacent check.
branches.explanation: g6# checks Kh5 with the pawn. Kh7 protects both g6 and h6, f5 controls g4, h6 controls g5, and White’s own rook blocks h4. The extra queens cannot interpose against a pawn’s adjacent check.

exercises.prompt: Which side are you trying to win with here?
exercises.answer: Black. The practice position begins with Black to move and a checked forced mating sequence.

exercises.prompt: Why can’t the white king capture the pawn on g6 at the end?
exercises.answer: Black’s king on h7 protects g6. The other king flights are blocked by White’s rook or covered by Black’s pawns.

startContext: Begin after White Kxh3 at 99 seconds in the complete fourteen-piece diagram. The Black-to-move Rh1+/Kg4/f5+/Kh5/g6 mate is proved against every legal White response; both replies are forced. White’s two queens, rook and all surviving pawns are preserved. The earlier Qxf2 sacrifice and other king/rook defenses remain outside this later mating proof.
